items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: I wanted to be the next Sonny Rollins. He was my gut at that time.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was thinking about your sound and then the incredible breadth of saxophone sounds that have happened since the 20s. And so you’re in the lineage, you’re in the current lineage of what’s going on now. Because sometimes I wonder does it get harder to come up with your own sound? I mean how do you go beyond John Coltrane’s harmonic innovations and so if I can’t do that what can I do?

Yeah well I mean I had like a kind of musical mid-life crisis in grad school, that period where I was working really hard but kind of burning out at the same time. And it came from, I specifically remember the moment. I was second year grad school — I was a grad assistant so I was supposed to be one of the top people. I was getting paid to be in school. I was in charge of a quote unquote beginning jazz combo with some freshman in it. And in came this punk saxophone kid who played circles around me. He was twice…

unique sound, it was just truly seeking what I like. And that’s another thing with that whole honestly listening to yourself. I think more musicians, or a lot of musicians, need to be honest about what they truly like in music. It’s kind of like when I was a teacher and I was teaching some of these saxophone majors, they were majors in music. They wanted to perform for a living. And like let’s say it was a classical student. And I’d say, hey have you listened to this piece? What recordings do you like? And they…
